c.tagline: Calypso, carnival and Caribbean chaos on the Savannah's edge.

taxi.color: white/yellow-plate H-registered private taxis and route taxis
taxi.fareNote: Route taxis charge fixed shared fares by destination; private/hotel taxis negotiate a fixed price upfront since meters are not standard.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.St. Ann's: Hilton Trinidad and Conference Centre, St. Ann's

avoid.reason: Avoid Laventille, Beetham Estate and Sea Lots — high crime; caution downtown at night

hood_desc: Trendy strip of restaurants, rum shops and nightlife along Ariapita Avenue; best for younger travelers and nightlife-focused visitors who want to walk to bars and food.
Leafy, upscale residential area near the Queen's Park Savannah and the historic Magnificent Seven mansions; suits business travelers and those wanting quiet, central lodging.
Hillside district overlooking the Savannah with the Hilton and Botanical Gardens nearby; suits business travelers, conference-goers and those wanting resort-style comfort with skyline views.
Historic inner-city area next to the Savannah with guesthouses in colonial-era homes; good for budget-conscious travelers who still want a walkable, central base.
Affluent suburban valley north of the city with malls, guesthouses and easy hillside access; suits longer-stay visitors and families wanting a quieter, greener base with taxi access into town.
lodging: Courtyard by Marriott Port of Spain

water.note: Tap water is treated but infrastructure issues persist; bottled water is recommended for visitors.

transit.pay: PTSC buses are paid in exact cash (TT$ coins) or with a PTSC smart card at City Gate; maxi-taxis (privately operated shared vans identified by route-color bands) are paid in cash directly to the driver or conductor; Water Taxi ferry tickets are bought as tokens or passes at terminal booths.
transit.hours: PTSC buses and maxi-taxis run roughly 5am-10pm with reduced late-night/route-taxi options; Water Taxi runs limited weekday commuter schedules, not late-night.
transit.note: Maxi-taxis are the most common way locals get around, identified by a colored band (e.g., yellow for Port of Spain routes); route taxis (shared private cars) supplement this along fixed routes.

ferry: Water Taxi (Port of Spain to San Fernando)
T&T Inter-Island Ferry (Port of Spain to Scarborough, Tobago)

transit.m: Maxi-taxi to City Gate terminal (~45 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; 10% is appreciated at restaurants if service charge isn't already added, and rounding up for taxis/porters is common.
